findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed staff not using a barrier to shot the faucet after washing their hands. PIC was made aware of the proper procedures for hand washing. Ensure that staff follows the adequate procedures for handwashing to avoid recontaminating their hands in the process of making food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Employee was observed washing their hands and not utilizing a barrier to shut off the faucet, thus recontamination of the hands took place. Education was provided verbally to staff that a barrier is necessary to turn off the faucet which will prevent recontamination of the hands after being washed.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand washing sink was observed to not have disposable paper towels available. When discussed with employees and PIC, it was made aware that there are no paper towels available in the building to restock the dispensers due to supply issues. Paper towels were purchased and delivered to the facility and may be utilized on top of the paper towel dispenser as a temporary solution until the next shipment of paper towels is delivered to the facility to refill the dispensers. Ensure these paper towels are available for employee use and that they are used appropriately to not only dry hands, but also to act as a barrier between the hands and the faucet to turn it off.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: At the start of the inspection, sanitizer buckets were tested and recorded at 0ppm. Employees were made aware and were very quick to dump and fill the sanitizer buckets with fresh solution. The fresh solution was recorded at 150ppm QUAT. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are tested and changed at a frequency necessary to maintain the appropriate sanitizer concentration according to the labels. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The wall and surface of the triple sink edge near the wall is observed to have an accumulation of debris/residue. Ensure this area receives proper attention to detail when cleaning and that the surfaces of the equipment and the wall remain clean.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop was observed to be stored in the basin of the mop sink. This item needs to be placed in a air drying position either hanging on the wall, inverted in the sink, or in the top of the mop bucket to allow adequate air flow and prevent potential bacterial or pathogenic contamination.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Caulking of the triple sink was observed to be in a state of disrepair. It looks like caulking was applied at one point, however, it is no longer serving its purpose as the surface of the table is much lower than where the caulking is placed. Ensure the current caulking is removed and replaced with a fresh bead of caulking that creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The walk-in freezer is observed with excess dirt/food debris under the shelves on the floor. Ensure the walk-in cooler receives proper attention to detail when cleaning and that the dirt/food debris is removed at a frequency necessary to maintain a the facility clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: Facility lacked a CFM on duty during the inspection. GIven the medium risk category, a Certified Food Manager must be present at the facility during all hours of operation. 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: Facility lacked the employee health reporting agreements. A copy was on file with the facility, but it had not been filled out by the employees. PIC was instructed to ensure all employees fill out the agreement and these agreements are kept on file and readily available upon inspector request.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
4-301.14: The hood vent above the oven was observed to be dripping with grease. The facility currently does not seem to have a contracted hood cleaning company, but the PIC informed inspector the owner will clean the actual hood vents in the triple sink, but not inside the duct work. Ensure the facility acquires a company to clean the hoods in a timely fashion to prevent the accumulation of grease and to prevent potential contamination form the drips.
4-301.14: Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings.
